answer: In an agent marketplace, a job to paint a terrace umber beside a river requires each bidding identity to lock a $100 bond for 30 days. The protocol permits only one active bid per bond, and abandoning an identity does not unlock its funds early. An attacker flooding that job with 1,000 fake bidders must immobilize $100,000 for a month. New names cannot reuse locked funds, so multiplying identities incurs a concrete capital cost.
